idea: Seed: port of the production MLP + train_ann.

Attack the edge-stencil deficit (r2_u 0.135 vs 0.328 full-stencil): the parent imputes NaN→0 after standardization, which makes swath-edge padding indistinguishable from a genuinely mean-valued feature, so the net cannot discount padded stencil cells. I append the binary finiteness mask of every input column as extra features (72 → 144 inputs), leaving architecture, loss, and schedule untouched. Missingness indicators are a proven fix for informative-missingness in tabular nets and directly give the model the "which stencil cells are real" signal the diagnostics say it lacks.

Attack the late-test/temporal generalization gap: the parent's validation split is a uniform random 10%, so early stopping and the LR plateau schedule are tuned for interpolation within the training window, not for forecasting later cycles — which is exactly what the held-out test measures. Since rows are time-ordered (later rows = later in the mission window, all regions interleaved), I replace the random split with a contiguous temporal tail split: the last 10% of training rows become validation. This makes the stopping criterion a proxy for the actual test regime (later, unseen times), which should pick a checkpoint that generalizes forward in time instead of one that has begun to memorize the training window. Everything else — architecture, loss, imputation, schedule — is unchanged.

Attack the edge-stencil deficit (r2_u 0.186 vs 0.456 full-stencil), the parent's largest weakness. Unlike gen001_00 (which changed the imputed value and scored neutral), keep NaN→0 mean-imputation but append explicit binary missingness indicators (isnan per column) as extra inputs. After imputation, padded stencil cells are indistinguishable from cells genuinely at the feature mean, so the net is forced into one compromise mapping for both; validity flags let it learn a separate edge regime (e.g. rely on the center cell and valid neighbors, discount phantom zeros). Doubles input width to 144 — negligible compute/memory — and everything that measurably worked in the parent (temporal validation split, schedule, early stopping) is kept intact.

[wildcard] Wildcard: replace the flat MLP with a stencil-CNN that restores the spatial structure the flattener destroyed. Each row is reshaped (feature-major layout) into an 8-channel 3x3 image, and 8 per-feature validity-mask channels are concatenated (16x3x3 input), so the network sees WHERE in the window data is missing instead of just zeros — directly attacking the edge-stencil deficit (r2_u 0.186 vs 0.456 full-stencil) while weight-sharing across the window adds a translation prior for the flow-gradient features. Two 3x3 padded convs with GroupNorm feed a small MLP head; all of gen001_01's proven plumbing (NaN-aware standardization, temporal last-10% validation, masked MSE, ReduceLROnPlateau + early stop, time-budget checks) is kept, with an in-epoch budget check since conv epochs are slower.

Attack recency/drift (r2_u_late 0.344 vs 0.362 early): the parent permanently sacrifices the final 10% of the training window — the ~380k rows temporally closest to the test set — as a validation-only split, so the model never learns from the most test-like data. Keep the temporal validation split for early stopping and LR scheduling exactly as-is, but after restoring the best checkpoint, add a short low-LR (1e-4, fresh AdamW) fine-tune pass over the FULL window including the tail, capped at 2 epochs and budget-checked in-loop. This is the standard "refit on all data after model selection" step, aimed where it pays most here: the tail carries the freshest mesoscale state, so absorbing it should lift late-test R^2 without disturbing the proven early-stopping machinery.

Attack the edge-stencil deficit (r2_u 0.186 vs 0.456 full-stencil) — the parent's largest weakness — but differently from the two failed imputation-order attempts (gen001_00, gen001_02): instead of changing HOW NaNs are filled, tell the network WHERE they are. After NaN→mean imputation, a padded stencil cell is indistinguishable from a genuinely average ocean state, so the net silently extrapolates full-stencil dynamics onto swath edges. I append k*k=9 per-cell missingness fractions (mean of ~isfinite across the 8 feature copies of each cell, exploiting the feature-major layout) as extra inputs. These are exactly zero for the ~full-stencil majority — so interior behavior and all proven machinery (temporal val split, early stopping, schedule) are untouched — while giving the net an explicit signal to learn a separate edge regime, which should lift the edge bins without the interior regression the imputation-based attempts caused.

Graft the one measurably-proven improvement in the history — gen002_00's post-selection recency fine-tune (+0.010 over its parent) — into this lineage's missingness-flag variant, targeting the late-test deficit (r2_u_late 0.3447 vs 0.3633 early). The parent permanently withholds the last 10% of the training window (the rows temporally closest to the test set) as validation-only, so it never learns the freshest mesoscale state. Keep the temporal validation split, early stopping, and per-cell missingness flags exactly as-is; after restoring the best checkpoint, run a short low-LR (1e-4, fresh AdamW, ≤2 epochs, budget-checked in-loop) fine-tune over the full window including the tail. If the fine-tune's gain is roughly orthogonal to the flags' edge-stencil signal, this variant should recover and exceed the parent's lost ground on late-test R^2.

[wildcard] Wildcard: replace the flat MLP with a gated mixture-of-experts over flow regimes, attacking the fast-regime deficit (rmse_speed_fast 0.241 vs 0.065 slow). A single MLP averages its capacity across slow background flow (most rows) and energetic fronts/eddies (few rows, huge variance), so the fast regime is underfit. The MoE has a shared trunk, a softmax gate, and 4 expert heads; the gate can route energetic-flow rows (large geostrophic anomalies in the input) to specialists while a "background" expert handles quiescent rows, without any hand-made regime labels. A small KL-to-uniform load-balance penalty on the mean gate keeps experts from collapsing to one. All proven plumbing from gen002_00 is kept unchanged: NaN-aware standardization, temporal-tail validation for early stopping, masked MSE, and the post-selection low-LR recency fine-tune.

Parent gen000_00 lacks the two proven wins in history, so first graft them from the inspiration: the temporal (last-10%) validation split (+0.009 fitness on this lineage) and the post-selection low-LR full-window recency fine-tune (+0.010 more). The one new focused change on top: maintain an exponential moving average (decay 0.999) of the weights, do validation/early-stopping/checkpointing on the EMA weights, and predict from the EMA after the fine-tune. Averaged weights flatten the sharp minima that SGD noise leaves in single-checkpoint models, which is exactly the failure mode of forward-in-time generalization — it should lift late-test R^2 further and stabilize the validation-free fine-tune pass, at near-zero compute cost.

Add EMA (exponential moving average) weight averaging to the parent, targeting the temporal-drift weakness (r2_u_late 0.3513 vs 0.3605 early) that the recency fine-tune only partly closes. SGD's final iterates bounce around the loss basin; averaged weights sit nearer the basin center, which is a well-established generalization gain that should specifically help forward-in-time transfer where the training-window optimum is slightly off from the test-window optimum. Concretely: maintain an EMA of all parameters (decay ramping to 0.999, ~1 epoch horizon), do validation/early-stopping/LR-scheduling on the EMA weights so model selection picks the averaged solution, and keep the EMA running through the recency fine-tune — where it doubles as a safeguard, since that phase has no validation signal and currently ends on whatever the last noisy mini-batches dictate. Everything else (missingness flags, temporal split, fine-tune schedule) is unchanged; the cost is one small in-place weight update per step.

Graft the single proven win in the history — gen002_00's post-selection recency fine-tune (+~0.014 fitness over its parent) — into this parent, keeping the parent's missingness-indicator channels intact. The parent's temporal early-stopping split permanently withholds the last 10% of the training window, the rows temporally closest to the held-out test cycles; after restoring the best checkpoint, a short fresh-AdamW low-LR (1e-4) pass over the full window (tail included, ≤2 epochs, budget-checked in-loop) absorbs the freshest mesoscale state without disturbing model selection. This directly targets the parent's late-test deficit (r2_u_late 0.349 vs 0.356 early) and composes orthogonally with the indicator features, which target the edge-stencil bin — testing whether the two wins stack.

[wildcard] Wildcard: replace the plain MSE-trained MLP with a heteroscedastic joint head — the trunk now predicts (mu_u, mu_v) plus per-row, per-component log-variances, trained with a masked Gaussian NLL. Motivation from the diagnostics: edge-stencil rows (r2_u 0.198 vs 0.453 full-stencil) and fast-regime rows (RMSE 0.241 vs 0.065 slow) are intrinsically noisier/harder, and under flat MSE they inject large gradients that distort the fit on the well-conditioned majority. Learned aleatoric variance lets the network自动 downweight those rows in proportion to their irreducible error, which typically raises average R^2 on temporally held-out data. Model selection and LR scheduling still use masked MSE on mu (the actual scored quantity), the logvar head is bias-initialized near the target log-variance for stable early training, and all proven plumbing from the parent (NaN-mean standardization, last-10% temporal validation, post-selection low-LR recency fine-tune) is kept intact.

Attack the edge-stencil deficit, the parent's widest diagnostic gap (r2_u 0.197 edge vs 0.454 full-stencil, r2_v 0.257 vs 0.533): the parent imputes NaN stencil-padding cells with the global feature mean (0 after standardization), which fabricates large artificial spatial gradients between a valid center cell and its mean-filled neighbors — exactly the gradient signal a stencil model reads as flow structure. Change the imputation to center-cell replication: reshape to (n, features, cells) and fill each NaN cell with that row's center-cell value of the same feature, so edge rows present a locally plausible, zero-gradient neighborhood instead of a global-average discontinuity. The per-cell missingness flags are kept so the network can still tell replicated padding from a genuinely uniform field, and everything else (temporal validation split, early stopping, proven recency fine-tune) is untouched.

Attack the edge-stencil deficit again — still the parent's widest gap (r2_u 0.198 edge vs 0.456 full-stencil) even after center-fill, because true edge rows are a minority of training data so the network barely practices the partial-neighborhood regime. Add edge-simulation augmentation: during training (main loop and fine-tune), a random ~25% of rows in each batch get a realistic swath-edge mask (one side or one corner of the k×k stencil) applied on-GPU using exactly the parent's convention — masked cells are overwritten with the row's standardized center value and the corresponding missingness flags are raised. This turns the abundant full-stencil rows into a large training signal for the edge regime, teaching the net to fall back gracefully to center-dominated predictions when flags fire, while leaving validation, fine-tune targets, and test inputs untouched. Everything else (featurization, temporal split, recency fine-tune) is kept verbatim from the parent.

Attack the remaining variance/drift weakness with a guarded two-seed deep ensemble — the one reliable-gain lever the history has not tried (weight-space EMA failed in gen003_01, but prediction-space averaging of independently trained nets is a different, stronger mechanism: it cancels seed-dependent errors, which shows up mostly in the noisy late-test and fast-regime bins). The parent trained in 377s, well under budget, so there is headroom: each member gets a hard per-member time slice (deadline at 0.95·(m+1)/M of the budget), trains with its own seed and permutation stream, keeps the parent's temporal-validation early stopping and the proven recency fine-tune inside its slice, and predictions are averaged. A safety guard drops any member whose best validation loss is >15% worse than the best member (e.g. a second model starved by a tight budget), so the worst case degenerates to exactly the parent's single model rather than polluting the average with an undertrained net. Everything else — featurization, missingness flags, architecture, optimizer, fine-tune — is byte-identical to the parent.

[wildcard] Wildcard: replace the flat MLP with a stencil CNN. The 72 inputs are 8 base features × a 3×3 spatial neighborhood, but the parent's MLP sees them as unordered columns and must relearn spatial structure (SSH gradients, shear, fronts) independently per feature. I reshape each row into an (F+1)-channel 3×3 image — the extra channel is the per-cell missingness map, giving edge padding an explicit spatial encoding — and apply two padded 3×3 convs (shared weights across positions = built-in derivative/curvature operators) before a small dense head. This targets the fast-regime RMSE deficit (0.2405, front/eddy dynamics are gradient-dominated) and the edge-stencil gap (spatial mask channel lets convs condition on WHERE padding sits, not just how much). Data plumbing is inherited unchanged from the parent: NaN-aware standardization, temporal 10% validation tail, early stopping, and the proven low-LR recency fine-tune; single model instead of the ensemble so the structural comparison is clean within budget.

Graft the inspiration's proven center-cell imputation into the two-seed ensemble parent, attacking the still-widest diagnostic gap: edge-stencil rows (r2_u 0.198 edge vs 0.455 full-stencil, r2_v 0.260 vs 0.535). The parent fills NaN stencil padding with the global feature mean (0 after standardization), fabricating large artificial spatial gradients between a valid center cell and mean-filled neighbors — exactly the gradient signal a stencil model reads as flow structure. gen004_00 showed center-cell replication (fill each NaN cell with that row's center value of the same feature, keeping per-cell missingness flags) beats mean-fill (+0.0011 over its single-model baseline); the ensemble (+0.0016) is an orthogonal variance-reduction lever, so the two gains should compose. Everything else — temporal validation split, early stopping, recency fine-tune, member deadline slicing, undertrained-member guard — is untouched.

Attack the persistent u-component deficit (r2_u 0.359 vs r2_v 0.434, in every bin): the harness scores mean-of-R², but the parent's masked MSE sums raw squared errors over both components, so the higher-variance component's residuals dominate every gradient step and the loss is not the metric. Reweight the loss per component by the inverse training variance of each target (normalized so total scale is unchanged), applied consistently in training, validation selection, and the recency fine-tune — this makes the optimized quantity a masked mean of per-component normalized MSEs, i.e. exactly (2 − R²_u − R²_v) up to constants, pulling gradient capacity toward the under-fit u channel. Everything else — center-cell imputation, missingness flags, temporal validation, two-seed guarded ensemble, fine-tune — is byte-identical to the parent.

Attack the fast-regime deficit (rmse_speed_fast 0.2405 vs 0.0653 slow), the diagnostic axis no lineage has touched yet: fronts and eddies — where flow is fast — are exactly where the ocean state varies sharply across the 3×3 stencil, but the MLP only sees raw cell values; spatial standard deviation is a nonlinear function of the inputs a first linear layer cannot form. Append one per-feature stencil standard deviation (computed on standardized values, NaNs ignored) as 8 extra inputs — an explicit front/eddy-intensity signal that also stays honest at swath edges (computed over valid cells only, with the existing missingness flags disambiguating). Everything else in the parent — mean-fill, temporal validation, recency fine-tune, two-seed ensemble, member guard — is untouched, so this isolates the feature-engineering lever from gen005_00's imputation lever for a later composition.

[wildcard] Wildcard: gated mixture-of-experts over flow regimes. The lineage's single shared MLP must average one set of weights across a heavily imbalanced flow distribution — slow, quiet ocean dominates the rows, so the fast regime (fronts/eddies) is fit as an afterthought and shows ~4x the RMSE (0.2352 fast vs 0.0655 slow). I keep the parent's proven plumbing (standardize + missingness flags + stencil-std features, temporal 10% validation, recency fine-tune, masked MSE) but replace the predictive core: a shared trunk feeds a softmax gate and 4 small expert heads, with the output a gate-weighted mixture and a small load-balance penalty so experts don't collapse onto the majority regime. The gate can route energetic-neighborhood rows (high stencil std, large geostrophic anomalies) to experts free to learn large-amplitude dynamics without being dragged toward the quiet-ocean mean, which is exactly the specialization a monolithic net cannot express. Single model with the full time budget instead of the two-seed ensemble, since the new core is the experiment.

Graft the inspiration's proven featurization — per-cell missingness fractions plus per-feature stencil standard deviations (computed on standardized values over valid cells only) — into the heteroscedastic-NLL parent, leaving its loss, temporal validation, and recency fine-tune untouched. This targets the parent's two widest diagnostic gaps at once and synergizes specifically with this lineage: the edge-stencil deficit (r2_u 0.206 vs 0.444 full-stencil) because the missingness flags let the model distinguish swath-edge padding from a genuinely mean-valued ocean, and the fast-regime deficit (rmse 0.2411 fast vs 0.0702 slow) because stencil std is an explicit front/eddy-intensity signal the first linear layer cannot form from raw cells. Crucially, these same inputs feed the logvar head, so the variance model can finally condition on the exact factors (edge rows, sharp fronts) it exists to downweight — the parent's heteroscedastic weighting was flying blind to them.

Graft the proven featurization from gen006_00 (the leaderboard's biggest single win, +0.036 over its parent) into this MSE-lineage parent, changing nothing else: replace the d-wide binary missingness block with the compact per-cell missing-fraction block (C columns) and append per-feature stencil standard deviations computed on standardized values over valid cells only (F columns). This directly attacks this parent's two widest diagnostic gaps — the edge-stencil deficit (r2_u 0.191 vs 0.446 full-stencil) because per-cell missing fractions encode swath-edge geometry far more learnably than 72 raw binary flags diluted through the first linear layer, and the fast-regime deficit (rmse 0.2422 fast vs 0.0665 slow) because stencil std is an explicit local-gradient/front-intensity signal the network cannot easily synthesize from raw cells. The featurization is also 73 columns narrower than the parent's, so epochs are cheaper and more of the time budget goes to training. Loss, temporal validation, early stopping, and the recency fine-tune stay exactly as in the parent, isolating the featurization as the single tested variable in this lineage.

Graft the inspiration's proven heteroscedastic NLL loss into the parent's two-seed ensemble, changing nothing else. The two lineages have each validated one half of this combination on identical featurization: gen006_00 (hetero-NLL, single net) scored 0.4224 while the MSE single-net equivalent lineage sat lower, and the parent's two-seed averaging is its own proven +variance-reduction lever. The NLL's per-row learned variance downweights exactly the parent's two weakest bins — edge-stencil rows (r2_u 0.285 vs 0.447 full-stencil) and fast fronts (rmse 0.2352 vs 0.0655 slow) — because the appended missingness and stencil-std features give the logvar head direct sight of those factors; ensembling then cancels the seed noise of two independently learned variance surfaces. Model selection and the member-quality guard stay on masked MSE of mu, the scored quantity, so the variance term never distorts early stopping or member acceptance.

[wildcard] Wildcard: replace the flat MLP core with a small CNN over the spatial stencil. Each row is reshaped feature-major into an (F, 3, 3) image and concatenated with F per-feature validity-mask channels (NaN pattern as explicit input), so convolution learns spatial derivatives (shear, divergence, front orientation) directly instead of relying on the hand-built stencil-std scalar, and the mask channels let filters adapt at swath edges — attacking the edge-stencil deficit (r2_u 0.29 edge vs 0.46 full), the worst diagnostic axis. A center-cell shortcut feeds the raw point features past the conv trunk so point-wise information is not blurred. All proven plumbing is kept: NaN-aware standardization, temporal 10% validation, heteroscedastic masked NLL with MSE-based model selection, recency fine-tune, and the two-seed ensemble.

Attack the edge-stencil deficit (r2_u 0.2867 vs 0.4537 full-stencil, the parent's widest diagnostic gap) at the imputation level, changing nothing else. The parent fills padded stencil cells with the global feature mean (0 after standardization), so every swath-edge row gets a neighborhood that looks like "average ocean" bolted onto its real center values — a systematic distributional distortion exactly on the rows the diagnostics flag. Replace mean-imputation with center-cell fill: after standardization (and after computing the stencil-std block, which must still see the true valid cells), each missing cell is filled with that feature's center-cell value, so an edge row degrades gracefully toward "locally uniform field" instead of "half-average field"; only rows whose center is itself NaN fall back to the mean. The missingness-fraction block is kept unchanged, so the net (and its logvar head) still knows which cells were padded — the fill only removes the artificial mean-shift, not the information. This is orthogonal to the two-seed ensembling already validated in the inspiration lineage and can be grafted there next if it wins.

Graft the inspiration's proven two-seed deep ensemble into the parent, changing nothing else. The two levers are each validated on identical base featurization: the parent's center-fill imputation added +0.005 over gen006_00's mean-fill, and gen006_02's two-seed averaging of independently learned hetero-NLL nets added variance reduction over its single-net parent lineage. Independently seeded members make decorrelated errors — including in their learned variance surfaces — and mu-averaging cancels that seed noise; the benefit is largest exactly where single-net predictions are noisiest, the edge-stencil bin that remains the parent's widest gap (r2_u 0.2894 vs 0.4618 full-stencil). Per-member wall-clock slices, model selection on masked MSE of mu, and the member-quality guard (drop members >15% worse than the best) are carried over verbatim so a starved second member degenerates back to the parent instead of diluting it.

Attack the fast-regime deficit (rmse_speed_fast 0.2310 vs 0.0674 slow) and the edge-stencil gap through the loss, not the features: the parent's plain Gaussian NLL has a known pathology — gradient on mu scales as 1/sigma^2, so exactly the rows the variance head flags as hard (fast fronts/eddies, padded edge stencils) get their training signal crushed by up to ~200x within the clamp range, undertraining the bins that dominate the squared-error budget. Switch to beta-NLL (Seitzer et al., beta=0.5): multiply each component's NLL by stop-grad(sigma^(2*beta)), so the mu-gradient scales as 1/sigma — interpolating between NLL (beta=0) and MSE (beta=1). This keeps heteroscedastic downweighting and calibration but restores signal on high-variance rows; weights are normalized per batch (weighted mean) so the loss scale and LR schedule stay comparable to the parent. One function changes; architecture, center-fill featurization, temporal validation, recency fine-tune all carried verbatim.

[wildcard] Wildcard: replace the flat MLP core with a gated mixture-of-experts over flow regimes, targeting the fast-regime deficit (rmse_speed_fast 0.2304 vs 0.0670 slow). A single MLP must fit one smooth function across calm shelf water and energetic fronts/eddies, so the majority slow-flow rows pull the fit away from the rare fast rows. Here a shared trunk feeds a softmax gate and K=4 small experts; the gate — conditioned on the same features that flag regime (geostrophic magnitudes, per-feature stencil std from the parent's featurization) — softly routes each row, so one expert can learn the steep fast-front mapping without being averaged into the calm-ocean fit. A small load-balance penalty prevents gate collapse. Everything else is the parent's proven plumbing unchanged: center-fill + missingness + stencil-std featurization, temporal 10% validation, masked-MSE selection, recency fine-tune, two-seed ensemble with the undertrained-member guard. Loss is plain masked MSE (no heteroscedastic head) so the run measures the MoE structure cleanly.

Attack the edge-stencil deficit (r2_u 0.2898 vs 0.4565 full-stencil, the parent's widest gap) with train-time stencil-dropout augmentation — a different mechanism than the inspiration's center-fill imputation. Real swath-edge rows are rare in training but common enough in test to drag the score; for a random 25% of training rows we simulate them by dropping ~half of the non-center stencil cells (zeroing their standardized values, exactly what test-time mean-fill produces, and setting their missing-fraction entries to 1 so the net can condition on the padding). The abundant full-stencil rows thus teach the net a mapping that stays calibrated when a neighborhood is padded, instead of edge behavior being learned only from the few genuine edge rows. Validation stays clean, augmentation is applied in both the main loop and the recency fine-tune for consistency, and everything else — hetero-NLL, two-seed ensemble, temporal val, member guard — is carried verbatim.

Attack the fast-regime deficit (rmse_speed_fast 0.2310 vs 0.0674 slow) through featurization — the lineage's proven lever (gen006_00's miss+std block gained, while gen007_02's loss-based fast-regime attack lost) — by appending per-feature directional stencil gradients. The existing spatial-std block is isotropic: it says "how much local variation" but not which way. I add zonal and meridional first differences across the k×k window (2F new features), computed after center-fill so swath-edge rows degrade to zero gradient (locally uniform, the physically neutral assumption). These are exactly the missing front/eddy dynamics: SSH gradients encode geostrophic shear, velocity-component gradients encode vorticity/strain — the quantities that distinguish a fast frontal jet from calm ocean with the same point values. Everything else (center-fill, hetero-NLL, temporal val, recency fine-tune) is carried over verbatim from the parent.

Attack the parent's widest diagnostic gap — edge-stencil r2_u 0.1969 vs 0.4538 full-stencil — by grafting the lineage's proven featurization upgrade into the parent's `_featurize`, changing nothing else. Two validated ingredients travel together from gen006_00/gen007_00: (1) per-feature stencil standard deviation over valid cells (an explicit front/eddy intensity signal that also helps the fast-regime bin, rmse 0.2407), and (2) center-fill imputation of missing stencil cells instead of mean-fill — mean-fill welds an "average ocean" neighborhood onto every swath-edge row, a systematic distortion on exactly the rows scoring worst; center-fill degrades them toward "locally uniform field", the physically neutral assumption, while the existing missingness block still marks which cells were padded. This featurization was worth ~+0.03 on an otherwise-identical lineage (gen003_03 → gen006_00 → gen007_00) and is orthogonal to the parent's loss, architecture, temporal validation, and recency fine-tune, which are kept verbatim.

[wildcard] Wildcard: replace the flat MLP trunk with a tiny stencil-CNN. Each row's 72 stencil columns are reshaped (feature-major layout) into an 8-channel 3x3 image, with the per-cell missingness fractions stacked in as a 9th channel, and processed by a small conv net (3x3 conv with padding -> 1x1 mixing conv -> 3x3 valid conv), whose 128-d embedding is concatenated with the per-feature stencil-std auxiliaries and fed to the mu/logvar heads. Weight-sharing across stencil positions gives the model an explicit, translation-consistent notion of local spatial gradients and shear — exactly the front/eddy structure behind the fast-regime deficit (rmse 0.2304 fast vs 0.067 slow) that a flat MLP must re-learn per-position — and the missingness channel lets the convolution see *where* the swath edge is inside the neighborhood, attacking the edge-stencil gap spatially rather than statistically. All proven plumbing is kept verbatim: center-fill featurization, heteroscedastic NLL, temporal-tail validation, recency fine-tune, and the two-seed ensemble with per-member wall-clock slices.

Add weight-EMA (Polyak averaging, decay 0.999) to each ensemble member — an untried, near-free variance-reduction lever orthogonal to everything proven in this lineage (the failed gen008 attempts all touched featurization or architecture; this touches only the optimization endpoint). Per epoch we validate both the raw and the EMA weights and keep whichever scores better on the temporal-val masked MSE, so the change is guarded: it can only match or beat the parent's selection. EMA finds flatter, temporally smoother minima than any single SGD iterate, which is exactly what a temporally held-out test rewards (the parent's late-test r2_u 0.3861 trails early 0.3987), and it also smooths the blind 2-epoch recency fine-tune — currently the only unvalidated stage — by replacing its arbitrary final iterate with the average along the fine-tune trajectory. The gain should stack with (not duplicate) the two-seed ensemble, since EMA averages within a trajectory while the ensemble averages across seeds.

Attack the edge-stencil deficit (r2_u 0.2898 vs 0.4565) at the loss level: the heteroscedastic NLL and the scored metric disagree. The variance head assigns edge/fast rows a high logvar, which shrinks their gradients by exp(-logvar) — up to ~250x under the clamp — so the net systematically underfits exactly the bins where R^2 (which weights all rows equally) is worst; stencil-dropout (gen008_00) failed because it added noise without restoring gradient. I add a small unweighted masked-MSE anchor to the NLL (loss = NLL + 1·MSE): for typical rows (logvar ≈ -3.5, precision ≈ 33) the anchor is a ~6% perturbation and calibrated downweighting is preserved, but on downweighted hard rows it restores a gradient floor ~15x larger than the NLL term, forcing the mu head to keep fitting edge and fast-front rows instead of explaining them away as noise. I also graft the inspiration's proven center-fill imputation (+0.005 on identical featurization) so the anchor acts on the better-conditioned edge inputs; ensemble, model selection on masked MSE of mu, recency fine-tune, and the member-quality guard are carried over verbatim.

Continue the lineage's proven imputation axis (mean-fill → center-fill gave +0.005) with one further physical refinement targeting the still-widest diagnostic gap (edge-stencil r2_u 0.2916 vs 0.4674 full): replace zero-gradient center-fill with gradient-preserving linear extrapolation. For a missing stencil cell, the point-reflected cell across the center is usually valid (swath edges truncate one side of the neighborhood), so fill with 2*center − mirror — the first-order Taylor continuation of the local field — instead of flattening the neighborhood to "locally uniform". This hands edge rows a physically consistent gradient (exactly the signal the spatial-std block and geostrophic features encode) rather than erasing it; fills are clamped to ±4σ in standardized units to stop noise amplification, and cells whose mirror is also missing fall back to center-fill, so the change strictly degrades toward the parent. Missingness flags and the valid-cell spatial std are computed before filling, unchanged.

[wildcard] Wildcard: replace the flat heteroscedastic MLP with a soft mixture-of-experts gated over flow regimes.
